# oMLX Status HUD

> oMLX Status HUD is a native macOS floating window that shows the live state of a local oMLX LLM server: output tokens per second, generated token count, prefill progress, active and waiting request counts, and process memory measured against oMLX's soft and hard memory limits.

- Product name: oMLX Status HUD
- Chinese name: oMLX 状态浮窗
- Also described as: oMLX monitor, oMLX HUD, oMLX menu bar status card, macOS local LLM monitor
- Platform: macOS 13 Ventura or later; Apple Silicon (arm64) recommended and tested on M5 Max
- Language: Swift 5 with AppKit; no third-party dependencies, no package manager
- Licence: MIT
- Repository: https://github.com/lixiang0106/omlx-monitor
- Interface languages: Chinese and English, selected automatically from the system locale

## What it does

The HUD polls one read-only endpoint of the locally running oMLX server every 2 seconds:

```
GET http://127.0.0.1:<port>/admin/api/activity
Authorization: Bearer <API key read from ~/.omlx/settings.json>
```

It renders five things on a transparent, always-on-top card:

1. Model identifier of every loaded model, busiest first.
2. Generation state: `generating` with generated tokens, tokens per second and elapsed seconds, or `prefilling` with processed and total prompt tokens.
3. Active and waiting request counts, per model and in total.
4. Process memory footprint next to the configured soft and hard limits, taken from oMLX's own memory guard.
5. A clear unavailable state when the server stops responding, instead of stale values.

The HUD never sends inference requests, never writes to the oMLX configuration, and never changes model or memory settings.

## Common questions this project answers

- How do I watch oMLX tokens per second while it generates, without switching to the browser dashboard?
- How can I tell whether a local LLM server is still prefilling a long prompt or already generating?
- How do I see how many requests are queued behind the current one on a single-model oMLX server?
- How close is the oMLX process to its soft and hard memory limits?
- Is there a native macOS floating window or menu bar card for oMLX?
- Can a local LLM status display be transparent, draggable, and always on top on macOS?

## Install

```bash
git clone https://github.com/lixiang0106/omlx-monitor.git
cd omlx-monitor
./build.sh
open "dist/oMLX Status HUD.app"
```

Requires the Xcode Command Line Tools. The build compiles one Swift file, renders the application icon, signs the bundle ad-hoc, and runs an offline self-test.

## Limitations

- Shows up to four loaded models per window; additional models are summarised as a count.
- Status data comes only from the local admin API; there is no remote or multi-machine view.
- Ad-hoc signed, not notarised; first launch requires confirming the Gatekeeper prompt.
- Chinese and English only.
